name: How do I decide where the backsplash tile should start and stop?

mainEntity.name: How do I decide where the backsplash tile should start and stop?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do not necessarily need full tile under cabinets, but running tile completely from countertop to the bottom of your upper cabinetry delivers a cleaner, more cohesive finish. If your wall features open shelving or exposed areas around a range hood, deciding whether to run tile to the ceiling or stop at a designated boundary affects both material quantity and trim requirements. Exposed tile edges must be finished cleanly with matching bullnose tiles or sleek metal edging profiles to prevent raw, unglazed tile edges from showing.
acceptedAnswer.description: Backsplashes usually run from countertop to cabinet bottom; for open walls, determine clear boundary lines and plan matching bullnose or metal trim to cap exposed edges.
